docs.title: Sankhara
docs.text:
Sankhara is a nation builder without wars, lived one person at a time. Each turn is a year. You act as one character, with a few slots of attention and whatever budget your station gives you: the treasury if you rule, your household if you farm, trade or teach. Events arrive, some of them asking something of you. When you die, the nation carries on and you begin again somewhere within it.

The ideas behind it are in Concepts; how they are built is in Architecture.

Status

Milestone 1 (the core loop) is playable: yearly turns, six stations, events and obligations, lives, succession and continuing in a new life. Research, policy and territorial growth come in Milestone 2; detailed NPC relationships and court politics in Milestone 3.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
uv sync
uv run sankhara        # or: uv run python -m sankhara

Choose New Game. Click a slot under Your attention to decide what the year is for, then End the Year. The game saves itself every year; Continue picks up where you left off.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
All code lives in the sankhara package under src/. The game is split into a pure-Python simulation (sankhara.sim, no Kivy, fully unit-tested and saveable) and a UI (sankhara.ui) that only reads state and calls a handful of game functions.

Package Responsibility sankhara.sim The game: state, rules, the yearly loop, lives and save/load. sankhara.world Map generation (map_gen.py) and hex-grid math (hexgrid.py). sankhara.core game_engine.generate_map(seed) builds the terrain. sankhara.entities Name generation per culture (namer.py). sankhara.ui Kivy screens: menu, game view, between-lives screen; theme.py palette and widgets; words.py turns numbers into the words the player sees. sankhara.constants config.py: map size, noise, biome thresholds and resources, culture groups. sankhara.app SankharaApp: screen flow and autosave.

docs.title: How the design maps to code
docs.text:
The design lives in Concepts. Milestone 1 implements the core loop:

Design Implementation One turn is one year game.end_year() advances the world one year, then begin_year() sets up the next. 2–3 action slots of personal attention stations.ACTION_SLOTS = 3; game.options(), choose(). A coarse budget the actions spend Budget(food, goods, coin). Rulers spend the national treasury; everyone else their household (actions.budget_for). Karma only on the action layer Each Action has a hidden karma value for its intention; skipped obligations subtract EventInstance.penalty. Outcomes never touch it. Stored on Soul.karma, clamped to [-1, 1]. Events, some random, some state-driven, not fair events.EVENTS: drought, plague, famine (when settlements go hungry), unrest (low stability), sick relatives, strangers… Meeting an obligation guarantees nothing. Lives of 20–50 turns, random death age Character.death_age is hidden: 16 + 20..50. Health can end a life sooner. Rebirth in the same nation, random station game.begin_next_life(): station drawn by Station.rebirth_weight; childhood is fast-forwarded to age 16. Karma shapes conditions, not rank At rebirth karma tilts carried-over tendencies (tendencies.carry_into_next_life), health, fortune (income), family_stability (family misfortune), parents' warmth, and which existing couple you are born to. Half of it is spent doing so. Tendencies, felt not shown tendencies.py: choosing an action strengthens its tags; declining a habitual default weakens them. Inclinations change costs (±30%), the order options appear in, their tint in the chooser, and which actions are pre-filled each year. NPCs, same model simplified npc.py: tracked adults choose station actions by tendency (rulers also by the realm's needs). Rulers' and nobles' choices act on the world. Upbringing and counsel pull others' tendencies toward the player's. Succession and lineage people.succeed(): eldest child, then sibling; if the line fails, an advisor founds a new house. No win condition The game runs until the player stops; it autosaves every year.

docs.title: Simulation modules
docs.text:
• state.py: dataclasses (GameState, Nation, Settlement, Character, Soul, Budget, EventInstance) with to_dict/from_dict. The RNG state is saved too, so a loaded game plays on identically.
  • game.py: founding a nation (capital on fertile interior land, a realm of radius 2, a few villages, a newly crowned ruler as the first life), the yearly loop, death and the next life.
  • actions.py: about 45 actions across six stations, plus generic and obligation-only actions. Each has a cost, tags, hidden karma and an effect function.
  • events.py: event definitions, yearly generation, obligation resolution.
  • nation.py: settlement economy (harvest falls as land fills up, taxes, hunger, growth), treasury upkeep and spoilage, drift of stability and prosperity, learning and arts with diminishing returns, household income and upkeep.
  • people.py: creating characters, families, ageing, marriage and births (tracked only for the ruler's line and the player's family), succession, keeping the court staffed.
  • stations.py, tendencies.py, npc.py, world.py (cached map per seed, fertility), save.py (JSON).

docs.title: World generation
docs.text:
1. Perlin noise produces elevation and moisture grids of MAP_WIDTH × MAP_HEIGHT, sampled at each hex's true position and normalised to [0, 1]. The game seed fixes the map.
  2. Each value is bucketed by ELEVATION_THRESHOLDS / MOISTURE_THRESHOLDS; the pair names the biome (e.g. "Hill Forest").
  3. Resources are seeded from BIOME_RESOURCE_BASELINES; a tile's fertility (plant food, animal food, fresh water) drives harvests.

docs.title: Hex grid
docs.text: world/hexgrid.py is pure math for a pointy-top grid in "odd-r" offset coordinates: centres, exact pixel-to-tile picking, corners, neighbours, distance and fitting a map to a box. The map view dims land outside the realm, outlines its border, marks settlements (capital in saffron) and outlines the player's home.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: The game's mechanics are meant to model a handful of Buddhist ideas. This page is a skeleton to be expanded from the original design conversation.

docs.title: Saṅkhāra
docs.text: Mental formations or volitional impulses: one of the five aggregates and the second link of dependent origination. In the game, the accumulated effect of a character's choices.

docs.title: Karma
docs.text: Intentional action and its consequences. Each turn's actions (and skipped obligations) adjust a karma score clamped to [-1, 1]; see ACTIONS in sankhara/constants/config.py.

docs.title: Rebirth and lineage
docs.text: A player is born into a Family on a home tile, which determines their culture group and names. Player.reincarnate() swaps in a new state (and optionally a new family); how karma drives rebirth is still to be designed.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• How karma maps to the next birth (species, family, location).
  • Whether NPCs share the same karma model.

docs.title: User Notes
docs.text:
• Original conversation is lost.
  • The game overall is supposed to be a nation builder that does not focus on war and army building. It's supposed to be a strategy game with resource mangament, policy/government management, scientific and cultural development but without armies and war being the main goal.
  • The Karma and rebirth cycle was inspired by the mechanics of the leader in games like Europa Universalis, in which the player is in charge of a country, but the leaders are born and die throughout the game, and lineage is an import aspect of holding power.

docs.title: Updated design direction:
docs.text:
Design summary

Premise. A nation builder with no focus on war or armies. Play centers on resource management, policy and government, and scientific and cultural development. Buddhist ideas (saṅkhāra, karma, rebirth) are modeled in the mechanics but never named or highlighted. There is no win condition, and the game runs until the player stops.

Turn structure. One turn is one year. The player acts as the current character, not as an abstract manager of the nation. Each turn has two layers: a fixed number of action slots (about 2 to 3) representing personal attention, and a coarse resource budget (a few categories) representing the nation’s capacity, which actions spend. Karma attaches only to the action layer: which actions are chosen and which obligations are skipped. Budget allocation affects the nation but not karma.

Events. Each year brings events, some random and some driven by the nation’s state. No attempt is made at fairness. Outcomes can be unjust or pointless. Events are the main source of obligations, and skipping them is penalized in karma. Karma tracks intention and choice, never outcomes.

Lifespan and lineage. A character’s life runs roughly 20 to 50 turns with a randomized death age, so the player cannot time final decisions. A full game spans several hundred turns and roughly 6 to 12 lives. Succession and lineage matter, as in Europa Universalis leaders.

Karma. Karma is a hidden score clamped to [-1, 1], never displayed as a number or label. Its only visible effects are felt ones.

Rebirth. Rebirth always stays within the same nation. Social station at rebirth is random, so players are not guaranteed to be rulers, and rank is not part of the karmic ledger at all. Every station has the same size of action set, with differing kinds and scopes of influence: a ruler’s is broad and slow, while a farmer’s or merchant’s is local and immediate. The design deliberately takes the position that status says nothing about worth. Karma governs the conditions within the station: mainly internal (tendencies), with smaller material (health, wealth within the station, family stability) and relational (parents, spouse, advisors, friends) adjustments. Becoming non-human is excluded from the main game, possibly reserved for an easter egg.

Tendencies (saṅkhāra). The past life’s habitual choices become the next life’s default impulses. They are never shown as labels or a character sheet and are only felt through the interface: some actions are cheaper in attention or resources, more prominent or tempting, or carry friction. The effect is a mild-to-moderate nudge that can always be overridden at a small extra cost. Effects must be consistent enough to be learnable. Tendencies shift throughout life at a constant rate: repetition strengthens them and acting against them weakens them, and the pattern at death is what carries into the next life.

NPCs. NPCs use the same model in simplified form, with tendencies that shift based on coarsely simulated choices. Rulers, heirs, advisors, and people near the player or in positions of power are tracked in detail, and the rest are handled statistically. Because rebirth stays in one nation, the people the player influenced remain, and the player can be reborn into the consequences of how they treated and shaped them.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Requires uv. The project is pinned to Python 3.12 (.python-version); uv will download it if needed.

uv sync                     # create .venv with runtime + dev dependencies
uv run pre-commit install   # run ruff and basic checks on every commit

docs.title: Common commands
docs.text: Task Command Run the game uv run sankhara Tests (with coverage) uv run pytest Lint uv run ruff check . Format uv run ruff format . All pre-commit hooks uv run pre-commit run --all-files Docs preview uv run --group docs mkdocs serve

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Tests live in tests/, mirroring the package layout (test_core/, test_world/, …). tests/conftest.py sets KIVY_NO_ARGS so Kivy doesn't consume pytest's arguments. UI tests need a display; CI runs them under xvfb-run.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: GitHub Actions runs lint and tests on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml), and publishes these docs to GitHub Pages on pushes to main (.github/workflows/docs.yml).
